a:r.a:t: Similar Mechanisms Introduce Carbonyls in Other Metabolic Pathways

p:cNvPr.descr: An image showing a conserved reaction sequence to introduce a carbonyl function on the carbon beta to a carboxyl group. This image has three columns. The first is beta oxidation. It begins with R bonding right to CH2 (blue box), which bonds right to CH2 (both CH2s are in a blue box), which bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to S-CoA. An arrow points down from this, with another curved arrow to the left, pointing to FADH2 in orange oval. Next is R bonding to CH, which double bonds right to CH (both CHs are in a blue box), which bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to S-CoA. Below this is an arrow pointing down, with H2O merging into the arrow. Next, R bonds right to CH, which bonds up to OH and right to CH2 (OH, CH, and CH2 are all in a blue box), which bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and down and right to S-CoA. Below this is an arrow pointing down, with another curved arrow to the left pointing to NADH in an orange oval. Next is R bonding right to C, which double bonded up to O and right to CH2 (O, C, and CH2 are all in a blue box), which bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and down and right to S-CoA. The next column to the right is the citric acid cycle. It begins with C double bonding up and left to O, down and left to O- and right to CH2 (blue box). CH2 bonds right to CH2 (both CH2s are in a blue box), which bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and down and right to O-. An arrow is below this pointing down. Another curved arrow to the left points to FADH2 in an orange oval. The next molecule is the same as the first, only instead of CH2, it has CH. Below this is an arrow pointing down, with H2O merging into it. Next, C double bonds up and left to O, down and left to O-, and right to CH (blue box). CH bonds up to OH and right to CH2 (all in a blue box), which bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and down and right to O-. Below this is an arrow pointing down. To the left is another curved arrow pointing to NADH in an orange oval. Below this, C double bonds up and left to O, down and left to O-, and right to C (in blue box). C double bonds up to O and right to CH2 (all in a blue box), which bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and down and right to O-. The next column is oxidation of isoleucine (leucine, valine). It begins with CH3, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH (where CH2 and CH are in a blue box). CH also bonds up to CH3 and right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and down and right to S-CoA. Below this is an arrow pointing down. To the left of this arrow is another curved arrow pointing to FADH2 in an orange oval. Next, CH3 bonds right to CH, which double bonds right to C (CH and C are both in a blue box). C bonds up to CH3 and right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and down and right to S-CoA. Below this is an arrow pointing down, with H20 merging into it. Next, CH3 bonds right to CH, which bonds up to OH and right to CH (both CHs and OH are in a blue box). CH bonds up to CH3 and right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and down and right to S-CoA. Below this is an arrow pointing down. To the left of this arrow is another curved arrow pointing to NADH in an orange oval. Next, CH3 bonds right to C, which double bonds up to O and right to CH (C, O, and CH are all in a blue box). CH bonds up to CH3 and right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and down and right to S-CoA.
